page.layout: One page of text, one column. Running head at top with the page number on the left. Heading in capitals with a Greek word and an italic line below it. Numbered paragraphs 1 to 4 follow. Catchword "dam" at the bottom right. No margin notes.

main_text.head: MULTIS MODIS HOMINES ψυχικὸς[?] observare vanitates mendaces, hæc inductio perspicuè ostendit.
main_text.p: 1. Amor mundi tantus in illis est, ut sint κοσμοι[?] in mundo. Iac.4.4. Adulteri & adulteræ, nescitis amicitiam mundi, inimiciti-am esse cum Deo? Quicunque ergo vo-luerit amicus esse mundi, inimicus Dei constituitur.
2. Idolomania in illis tanta est, ut quidam illorum dicant ligno, Pater meus es tu: & lapidi, Tu me genuisti. nam obvertunt Jehouæ cervicem, & nō faciem. Jer. 2.27.
Cæteri paulò prudentiores, veritatem in iniustitia detinent, Deiq; veritatem mutant in mendaciu, & colunt seruiuntq; rebus creatis, &c. Rom.1.18.&25.

3. Terrenas quinetiam opes cœlestibus anteponunt, contra expressum Domini præceptum: Ne thesauros congerite in terra, ubi tinea & erosio corrumpit, & ubi fures perfodiunt & furantur. Sed congerite vobis thesauros in cœlo, &c. Matthæi 6.19.20.
4. Valetudinem prosperam, si Deus nō statim concedat, vel à Satana sibi peten-

page.notes: Greek words in the heading and the phrase κοσμοι are uncertain; the accents and letters may not match the printed form exactly. The word "dam" is the catchword, which completes "peten-". Woodcut-free page with some show-through at the edges, not transcribed. The long s in "thesauros" and "statim" was read as plain s.
